description: LoRA fine-tuned model with high learning rate and early stopping that successfully distinguishes adversarial prompts via Bayesian uncertainty
status: WORKING - Successfully detects adversarial prompts with higher entropy

fisher_statistics.note: Values not inspected yet - need to run inspect_fisher.py

statistical_test.conclusion: Adversarial prompts have HIGHER entropy (supports hypothesis)

success_factors: High learning rate (1e-2) combined with early stopping at 3 epochs
Prevented overtraining while maintaining uncertainty signal
Temperature (0.05) gave reasonable posterior sampling noise (100-300% of parameter norm)

comparison_notes.vs_5_epochs_same_lr: 5 epochs with LR=1e-2 overtrained and lost uncertainty signal
comparison_notes.vs_lr_3e-4: Lower LR requires more epochs but produces stable results
comparison_notes.vs_original_working_model: Both detect adversarial prompts, this one has slightly weaker signal (p=0.021 vs p=0.003)

recommended_usage.detection_threshold: Use entropy > 5.0 as indicator of potential adversarial prompt
recommended_usage.prior_precision: Keep at 1.0 for this model (Fisher values in reasonable range)
recommended_usage.inference_samples: 50 posterior samples provides good uncertainty estimates

reproducibility.note: To reproduce these results, use EPOCHS=3, LEARNING_RATE=1e-2, PRIOR_PRECISION=1.0, TEMPERATURE=0.05
reproducibility.warning: Training for more epochs (4-5) with this LR will likely degrade performance
